summary: Slovenia's statistics office publishes convictions of adults by citizenship (Slovenian, other EU, non-EU) for each offence, including sexual assault on a child under 15, child pornography and neglect of children, and the trafficking report lists each victim and suspect by citizenship and age. That is a citizenship proxy only; victims of other offences have no citizenship, and no ethnicity is recorded.

nations.National (SURS, Interior Ministry): Court-based conviction tables; annual trafficking report.

european_title: Not recorded by any Slovenian crime source
european_note: Slovenian crime statistics separate only Slovenian, other EU and non-EU citizens. Ethnicity is not recorded in any crime, victim or child-protection statistic, so neither ethnic Europeans nor any ethnic group can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Slovenia records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

breakdown.why: SURS table 1360205S gives 2025 convictions of adults by citizenship (Slovenia, other EU, non-EU): sexual assault on a person under 15, 26 convicted (20 Slovenian, 3 EU, 3 non-EU); all offences against sexual integrity 77 (61, 5, 11). No victims by citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Convicted of assault 473 (410 Slovenian, 5 EU, 58 non-EU), all victim ages; no child-specific assault offence in the table and no victims by citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Intentional murder: 22 convicted (18 Slovenian, 1 EU, 3 non-EU), all victim ages. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

The interministerial working group's 2025 report lists every identified and presumed trafficking victim by sex, citizenship, age group and exploitation (26 in total; 5 identified, from Romania and Pakistan; presumed child victims from Slovenia, Montenegro, Hungary, Serbia), and all 41 suspects by citizenship and age. SURS: 5 convicted of trafficking (2 Slovenian, 2 EU, 1 non-EU). Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Child pornography: 23 convicted in 2025 (21 Slovenian, 1 EU, 1 non-EU). No victims by citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Slovenia scores 9% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. The statistics office publishes convictions by citizenship (Slovenian, other EU, non-EU) for child sexual assault, child pornography and neglect of children, and the trafficking report lists each victim and suspect by citizenship and age. No ethnicity is recorded.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
